answer: The protocol requires 1,000 units of compute-work per identity to prevent cheap flooding. The verifier acts as a beacon, rejecting any reused output or stale evidence. An honest agent pays this fixed cost, but an attacker needing 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 units, hitting a ferrous wall of processing exhaustion. This mechanism assumes no collusion exists among compute nodes. Like a shifting glacier that makes passage impossible without movement, the verifier forces unique work. Failure triggers immediate identity revocation. The cost is non-refundable and hard.
